turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The process route dominates everything.** Sorting by `target`, the data splits into clear process families:

| Family (signature) | target range |
|---|---|
| As-rolled/normalized only (THT=30, CT=30, TT=30) | 225–275 |
| Through-hardened + high-temperature temper (THT≈825–865, TT=550–680) | 325–643 |
| Through-hardened + low temper (TT=420–500, high C/Si) | 688–906 |
| **Carburized (NT=930, THT=30, CT=930, Ct>0, DT≈850–896, Dt>0, QmT>30, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5)** | **838–1190** |

Every one of the top ~30 samples is the carburizing route. So the recipe must copy that signature exactly: NT=930, THT=30 (no through-hardening), THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, DT≈850, Dt≈15, QmT high, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5.

**2. Within the carburized family**, secondary trends:
- Long carburizing time helps: the three best (1124, 1190, 1054–1056) use Ct≈470–540; Ct=90–130 rows sit at ~986–1074. → Ct=540.
- TT=160 ≥ TT=200 (matched pairs: 1144 vs 1104, 1082 vs 1035, 1089 vs 1053). → TT=160.
- DT=850/Dt=15 appears in the four highest (1034, 1054, 1056, 1082, 1124, 1190). QmT=140 slightly beats 60 in matched pairs (1190 vs 1124, 1030 vs 1028). → DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140.
- Alloying: the best heats are high Ni + Cr + Mo (Ni 1.62–1.69, Cr 0.45–0.59, Mo 0.16–0.21 → 1034–1190) or high Cr (Cr 1.14–1.17, Mo 0.17 → 1068–1144). Combining Ni≈1.7 with Cr≈0.8–0.9 and Mo≈0.2 is a mild, defensible interpolation of both winning branches.
- Low P and low S with low inclusion ratings (dB=dC=0) accompany the top rows (P=0.002–0.008, S=0.012–0.016); Mn low (0.51–0.62) in the best two. Base C ≈ 0.2 (carburized surface supplies the carbon), Si ≈ 0.35 (highest Si in the family, present in the 1124/1190 rows).
- RedRatio: 860 in the two top rows (1124, 1190), so keep 860.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.22, Si=0.35, Mn=0.55, P=0.002, S=0.012, Ni=1.7, Cr=0.85, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.2, RedRatio=860, dA=0.05, dB=0.0, dC=0.0**
